records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — A custom grant using the documented three-character shortcut produces token IDs that this decoder always rejects.
records.rationale: The finding claims that a custom grant using a three-character shortcut would be rejected by the decoder. Looking at the code in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java lines 68-85, the getTokenContextFromTokenId method checks `if (encodedContext.length() != 6)` and throws an exception. The encoded context is composed of sessionType shortcut (2 chars) + tokenType shortcut (2 chars) + grantType shortcut. The OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but the decoder expects exactly 6 characters total, meaning grant shortcuts must be exactly 2 characters.
